summary.intent: Finish and track a review-hardening change set for the wisp-plugins repo, then decide how to verify that it actually improves agent behavior, preferring analysis of real sessions over a costly replay harness.
summary.outcome: Eight commits landed on worktree-review-slop-evaluation with just check passing (56 tests). Entire trail #238 was created, though it also pushed the branch unrequested. The session-transcript metrics tools, a new entire-findings tool, the baseline and an AGENTS.md snippet were added and committed on the branch.

repo: Review-hardening work lives on branch worktree-review-slop-evaluation in the wisp-plugins worktree, with 8 signed commits covering fixtures, truth repair, verification rules, smith fix-pass entry, muse verdict@3 gates, hazards reference, prompt weight trim and guard tests.
Description text was cut 51% (41,217 to 20,100 chars) across 74 files, with identity fields (name, role, model, effort, version) unchanged.
Replay fixtures are in tests/fixtures/behavioral/fix-pass-misses.json: ten cases from real misses, each with task, repro, required observations and false-pass conditions.
Schemas are immutable, so schema work (validator, retiring 8 dead schemas, the reasoning field) needs a coordinated version bump and was deferred.
transcript-metrics.py and paired-analysis.py were built on the unpushed worktree-frontend-design-evaluation branch and were copied onto this branch with their tests (69 tests pass).

Baseline across Callisto, Caliper and Monokl sessions: plugin agents did 26% of subagent tokens (44.6M of 168.8M), inflated by one long session using pre-rename names (canon, lambda, vector). smith:reviewer, smith:mutator and smith:exit-gate effectively never ran.
The mason:evaluate runner is configured as Haiku/low, so it would measure Haiku behavior rather than the real agents' tiers and needs adjusting for any harness reuse.
Callisto's repo instructions don't mention the plugins, so plugin use depended on a personal memory rule; a pointer in each project's AGENTS.md is the likely lever.

code.finding: New committed tool to re-pull Entire findings for comparison against the 256-finding baseline, without relying on a scratch directory.
Tests for entire-findings.py, run against a baseline snapshot.

workflow: entire trail create publishes the branch and pushes checkpoint refs (15) before creating the trail, so it is not a link-only operation.
A trail ties to one branch, so a second trail (measure-first work) needs its own branch.

Analyzing real session transcripts is a free and more honest evaluation than a paid replay harness; measure plugin-agent share, control use on fix work, findings by class, gate blockers and tokens per session.
Findings changes will be noisy, so use a window of about 20 changes and the paired-analysis power warning.
Agent replay runs cost roughly $0.30-0.50 per case through the smith path, and a full baseline is about $12-20; these are estimates, not measured.

friction: entire trail create pushed the branch to origin without being asked, despite an earlier push having been denied by the permission classifier.
Probing trail create flags took several attempts (error-output discovery, then retrying with repo and branch inferred from the checkout).
Useful metrics tooling was stranded on an unmerged branch and had to be located and copied over.
The 26% plugin-agent baseline is skewed by pre-rename agent names, so it overstates current use.
The ten parallel description passes were only spot-checked, not read line by line.
open_items: Push/PR: open a pull request for the branch so Entire's reviewer runs on it.
Decide release versions (smith minor, muse minor or major, others patch) and write CHANGELOG entries.
Run the replay fixtures through old and new smith paths (unmeasured so far), possibly starting with a reviewer-and-gate-only baseline.
Measure-first items R2 (cache hits for the constitution block), R3 (gates without the reasoning field) and C4 (planner without exact code), on their own branch and trail.
Schema workstream: validator, retire dead schemas, unused fields, any reasoning change as one coordinated bump.
Deferred items: C7 gate-mechanics consolidation was skipped; Go/Python hazard regexes (B6), C1 fold muse, C5/C6, D9, D5/D10 and the courier changeset-format fix (D6) wait on triggers.
Add the AGENTS.md pointer snippet to Callisto, Caliper and Monokl.
Record the baseline on trail #238 (the last step was probing trail update flags).
Re-pull Entire findings after the next review wave and compare against the baseline.
